gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-fs-literata: Expressive, Balsamiq Sans cuts its line like a stencil channel, constant in weight and free of pinched curves. And it earns its keep big and short, while Literata's text serif hairlines stay sturdy beneath it.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-fs-sentient: Thick-thread lettering with no pinched curves: Balsamiq Sans traces one bold, steady line across every glyph. And Sentient, a serif whose stems outweigh its hairlines a little, is best given a modest size under a big heading.
gen-gf-baumans-fs-literata: A c shaped like an open crescent wrench marks Baumans, whose strokes all share a single thickness. Literata, a serif with sturdy hairlines and slightly heavier thick strokes, does the quiet reading; Baumans does the announcing.
gen-gf-baumans-fs-sentient: Sentient, a serif with pinched, closed-in apertures and crossbars a touch thinner than its stems, sits against Baumans' open letters. Baumans makes the commanding statement, and Sentient handles the finer explaining.
gen-gf-bellota-fs-literata: Distinctive in manner, Bellota hangs its s ends far from the spine. Make the heading small and its stylus-width strokes lose their authority, just as Literata, a serif, would sprawl if the body went large.
gen-gf-bellota-fs-sentient: Strokes that resemble a bent paperclip give Bellota its look, each traced at the width of one stylus. But Sentient, a text serif drawn with a barely tilted calligraphy nib, gives the wire-like heading a softer partner.
gen-gf-bellota-text-fs-literata: Bellota Text drops thick-thin shading entirely, leaving open, unguided letter shapes that command attention. Yet Literata, a text serif with a faint nib-pressure variation in each round letter, does the patient work.
gen-gf-bellota-text-fs-sentient: Commanding and open, Bellota Text leads the way. Sentient follows with closed-in, pinched letters and crossbars a touch thinner than stems, so a full page of it feels sophisticated and contemporary.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-fs-literata: Bruno Ace draws every line with a ruler, its counters staying connected to the outside, one character per lingering beat. Literata, a text serif with quiet modulation, makes reading feel unhurried.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-fs-sentient: Ruler-straight, unhurried lettering: Bruno Ace keeps its counters connected to the outside, one character per beat. Then Sentient, a text serif with closed-in apertures, tucks in tighter and sets up a pleasing push and pull.
